research_scope: Wave2 source-free review of generic mathematical prerequisites versus typed source-specific specializations; no promotion, source edits, gate, or human certification.

aliases.reason: Depth source takes the supremum of nonnegative lengths of M-regular sequences contained in an ideal. The underlying order operation is the least upper bound of the set of lengths in the ordered set ℕ∪{∞}, precisely the general poset-supremum construction. The extended value ∞, restriction to M-regular sequences, and containment in I remain defining source-context qualifications.

The finite-module-dimension source takes suprema of lengths of prime chains in Supp_R(M). These are least upper bounds in ℕ∪{∞} just as for any subset of an ordered set, with +∞ for unbounded integer lengths. The prime-chain restriction and support of M are parent-specific and do not become part of the abstract supremum prerequisite.

A finite rank free left R-module R^n is the finite-index direct sum of copies of R and hence the n-element-basis case of the generic free left R-module R^{(I)}. The finite-rank/standard-basis requirements for rank and Lazard, finite-presentation and finite-projective sources remain parent-specific; a free module of arbitrary rank is not assumed finite or locally free by this alias.

The splitting-field source's extension generated by F together with all roots of P in E is the general field-generation construction F(B), taking B to be the subset of roots. The target candidate defines k(B) as the least intermediate subfield containing the base field and B. Full splitting of P, root selection, and splitting-field minimality remain only in the parent construction.

The primitive-element source uses F(α), the smallest subfield containing F and a selected α, which is precisely k(B) for base k=F and singleton generator set B={α}. Rational expressions in α describe that generated subfield; its single-generator restriction and the primitive-element assertion are parent-specific, not imposed on arbitrary generated fields.
